Paragraph: Summary of Passage: Arjuna asks Krishna how He could have taught the sun-god Vivasvan in ancient times, given that Vivasvan was born long before Krishna's current earthly appearance.
Situation/Problem_Faced: Apparent chronological impossibility and confusion regarding human versus divine identity.
Key_Teaching/Action_Taken: Arjuna inquires: 'Aparam bhavato janma param janma vivasvatah...' (Your birth was recent, Vivasvan's was ancient; how am I to understand that You taught him initially?).
Outcome/Resolution: Prompts Krishna to clarify the difference between ordinary human existence and His eternal divine identity.

Mental_Health_Theme_Synonyms.Inquiry and Socratic Dialogue: Asking targeted questions to uncover deeper truth
Mental_Health_Theme_Synonyms.Challenging Apparent Contradictions: Testing logical consistency before accepting profound concepts
Mental_Health_Theme_Synonyms.Seeking Intellectual Clarity: Resolving doubt through direct, honest communication

Spiritual_Psychological_Concept_Indian.Concept: Aparam bhavato janma param janma vivasvatah (Your birth was later, Vivasvan's birth was earlier)
Katham etad vijaniyam (How am I to comprehend this?)

Brief_Summary_Spiritual: Arjuna questions Krishna on behalf of future generations, asking how Krishna could have instructed the ancient sun-god Vivasvan when He appears as a contemporary.
Brief_Summary_Psychological: Constructive questioning is essential for psychological growth; expressing doubts openly allows one to move past cognitive confusion toward meaningful conviction.
